sources.citation: Paul Broca (2011). Remarks on the Seat of Spoken Language, Followed by a Case of Aphasia (1861). Neuropsychology Review. [English translation of Paul Broca's April 18, 1861 Bulletins de la Société Anatomique de Paris report on Louis Victor Leborgne ('Tan')]
sources.notes: Foundational primary work — 1861 original Bulletin de la Société Anatomique clinical report (2011 English translation) — establishing the core empirical observations and theoretical framework.

sources.citation: Evelina Fedorenko, Idan A. Blank (2020). Broca’s Area Is Not a Natural Kind. Trends in Cognitive Sciences.
sources.notes: Fedorenko & Blank (2020 Trends in Cognitive Sciences) functional neuroimaging reassessment dissociating language-selective vs domain-general subregions inside Broca's area.

sources.citation: Francis Schiller (1983). Paul Broca and the history of aphasia. Neurology.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (1983) in Neurology extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: J. P. Mohr, M. S. Pessin, S. Finkelstein, H. H. Funkenstein et al. (1978). Broca aphasia. Neurology.
sources.notes: Landmark clinicopathological study demonstrating that lesions restricted solely to surface Broca's area cause transient mutism rather than permanent Broca's aphasia.

sources.citation: David A. Lee (1983). Paul Broca and the history of aphasia. Neurology.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (1983) in Neurology extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: N. F. Dronkers, O. Plaisant, M. T. Iba-Zizen, E. A. Cabanis (2007). Paul Broca's historic cases: high resolution MR imaging of the brains of Leborgne and Lelong. Brain.
